assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Yellow flame colour
items.clue: The flame colour produced by sodium compounds in a flame test.

items.label: Green flame colour
items.clue: The flame colour produced by copper compounds in a flame test.

items.label: Crimson flame colour
items.clue: The flame colour produced by lithium compounds in a flame test.

questions.stem: A student holds a small sample of an unknown ionic compound on a clean wire in a hot Bunsen flame, and a strong colour appears. What does the flame colour identify?

options.text: the metal ion, the cation, present in that compound
the negative ion, the anion, in the compound
the compound as a whole and not one of its ions
the temperature reached by the Bunsen flame

questions.explanation: Flame tests can be used to identify some metal ions (cations).

questions.stem: Lithium chloride is held on a clean wire in a hot Bunsen flame. What is seen?

options.text: The flame turns a bright yellow colour.
The flame turns a deep crimson colour.
The flame turns an orange-red colour.
The flame turns a pale lilac colour.

questions.explanation: Lithium compounds result in a crimson flame.

questions.stem: Sodium chloride is used in a flame test. Which statement describes the result?

options.text: Sodium ions colour the flame bright orange.
Sodium ions colour the flame orange-red.
Sodium ions colour the flame yellow.
Sodium ions colour the flame lilac.

questions.explanation: Sodium compounds result in a yellow flame.

questions.stem: Potassium bromide is tested in a flame test. What is the result?

options.text: The flame colour produced is yellow.
The flame colour produced is crimson.
The flame colour produced is orange-red.
The flame colour produced is lilac.

questions.explanation: Potassium compounds result in a lilac flame.

questions.stem: Calcium nitrate gives a distinctive colour in a flame test. Which colour is it?

options.text: a pale green flame colour
an orange-red flame colour
a bright crimson colour
a bright yellow colour

questions.explanation: Calcium compounds result in an orange-red flame.

questions.stem: Copper(II) sulfate is held in a hot Bunsen flame during a flame test. What is seen?

options.text: The flame is coloured a crimson red.
The flame is coloured pale blue.
The flame is coloured a bright green.
The flame colour does not change at all.

questions.explanation: Copper compounds result in a green flame.

questions.stem: A solution contains both sodium ions and potassium ions. In a flame test only a yellow colour is seen. Why is the lilac colour of potassium not seen?

options.text: The potassium ions are destroyed in the flame.
The two colours mix to give a new colour.
Potassium needs a hotter flame than this one.
The intense sodium colour masks the lilac.

questions.explanation: If a sample containing a mixture of ions is used some flame colours can be masked.

questions.stem: An unknown compound gives a yellow flame test colour. Its solution gives a white precipitate when dilute hydrochloric acid and then barium chloride solution are added. What is the compound?

options.text: sodium sulfate
potassium sulfate
sodium carbonate
sodium chloride

questions.explanation: The yellow flame shows sodium ions and the white precipitate with acidified barium chloride shows sulfate ions.
